milestone: Collection — Theme-Scoped, Deduplicated Asset Registry (Phase 4: Compile-Time Dedup in builder.js)
slice: Implements Phase 4 of the approved Collection plan -- the actual 'reduces data load' payoff, entirely inside tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js's existing convergeScenes -> convergeScene -> convergeSceneLayer -> externalizeSceneImage chain, no new UI. packageTheme() gains package_.collectionAssets = await this.collectFolder('collection') (the identical pattern already used for frameVariations/layerPack/representations -- metadata only, never itself holding embedded bytes; theme.collectionAssets on the compiled .vtheme is a separate, later phase). convergeScenes() builds one ref-keyed lookup (refToEntry) from that array, once per Build, threaded down as a new trailing parameter through convergeScene -> convergeSceneLayer -> externalizeSceneImage. Inside externalizeSceneImage, before computing today's per-Layer relPath ('scenes/<sceneId>/<layerId>.png'), a Layer's own layer.image is checked against refToEntry: a hit converges onto that entry's OWN stable key ('collection/<id>.png') instead of minting an independent relPath for every Layer -- so N Experiences/Layers sharing one Collection asset compile to exactly ONE embedded image in package_.assets, not N duplicates, the literal realization of the user's own words: 'the concept of collection allows reusable assets for creator and parallely reduces data load on builder by remapping to same asset used in different experiences.' A miss (a Layer whose image was never registered in Collection -- every Theme authored before this feature, or content Phase 1's auto-registration hook never saw) falls straight through to exactly today's per-Layer relPath, fully unaffected. A small memoization guard (skip re-hydrating via AssetStore.hydrateForExport() if package_.assets[relPath] is already set) avoids a redundant Storage round trip for every additional Layer sharing one Collection asset -- purely an efficiency guard, since writing the identical value to the same key twice would be harmless either way. A real bug was caught and fixed mid-implementation, before any test ever ran against it: convergeSceneLayer's own single call site to externalizeSceneImage (inside the layer.kind==='decoration' && layer.image branch) was updated for the new signature everywhere EXCEPT that one call itself, silently passing undefined for refToEntry and making the whole dedup path unreachable in practice -- caught by a follow-up grep across every externalizeSceneImage/convergeSceneLayer/convergeScene reference in the file before writing the verification suite, not by a failing assertion. Verified via a new, comprehensive Playwright suite (collection_phase4_verify.js, 17/17 assertions, zero console/page errors) driving the REAL, unmodified compile pipeline end to end -- ProjectCompiler.runBuild(project) -> validator.validate() -> builder.build() -> packageTheme() -- against a real Blank World Project with a real Scene: two real Experiences (both graduated Public, both Free-hosted, both mirrored onto DISTINCT Scene Layers via the real Engine Adapter) sharing the exact same Collection ref converge to EXACTLY ONE compiled collection/<id>.png asset (not two scenes/.../<layerId>.png duplicates), with BOTH compiled Layer Pack entries' decoration.image fields pointing at that same relPath; a third, legacy-shaped Decoration Layer authored directly (never through an Experience, never registered in Collection) alongside them still converges via exactly today's own per-Layer relPath, completely unaffected by Collection existing elsewhere in the same Theme -- confirming the fallback path is genuinely untouched, not just assumed so; and two consecutive Builds of the unmodified Project produce a byte-identical compiled assets map (both keys and values), matching this codebase's own already-established Publish determinism guarantee. Full regression: both goldenBuild.js suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) pass unchanged, confirming a Theme with zero Collection entries still compiles byte-identically to before this plan; the Phase 1 (27/27), Phase 2 (28/28), and Phase 3 (25/25) suites all pass completely unchanged, confirming zero regression from this phase's own additions. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; tools/world-builder/ (v1) and root Studio are completely untouched -- confined entirely to tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js. Phases 5 (Creator-facing availableToCreator metadata on the compiled .vtheme, with a docs/VTHEME_PACKAGE_SPEC.md update) and 6 (Creator-side 'From This World' browsing UI in js/contextPanel.js's Add Something accordion) remain named, not-yet-started increments -- see /root/.claude/plans/witty-floating-thimble.md for the complete phased rollout.
